p: My eiruv on the first … to the east, … and on the second … to the west. … On the first … to the west and on the second … to the east. … My eiruv … on the first … but on the second

My eiruv on the first day shall be to the east, and on the second day to the west. Alternatively, one may say: On the first day it shall be to the west and on the second day to the east. Similarly, one may say: My eiruv shall apply on the first day, but on the second
the inhabitants of my town, … My eiruv
on the second … but on the first
on the second day, but on the first
he either establishes an eiruv in one direction
or he establishes no eiruv at all; either he establishes an eiruv for
two days, or he establishes no eiruv at all.
What does one do … He … brings
What does one do to establish an eiruv that will be valid for both the Festival and Shabbat? He or his agent brings
and he stays … with it until nightfall, … and … he takes it … and goes away, … On … second … he stays … with it until nightfall, … eat

and he stays there with it until nightfall, the time when the eiruv establishes that location as his residence for the Festival, and then he takes it with him and goes away, so that it will not become lost before the following evening, in which case he would not have an eiruv for the second day. On the eve of the second day, he takes it back to the same place as the day before, and he stays there with it until nightfall, thereby establishing his residence for Shabbat, and then he may eat
and go away, … Consequently, … he benefits … walk … and he benefits … his eiruv.
and go away, if he so desires. Consequently, he benefits in that he is permitted to walk in the direction that he desires, and he benefits in that he is permitted to eat his eiruv.

p: you agree with me that … constitute two
you agree with me that Shabbat and a Festival constitute two
This is what the Rabbis said to Rabbi Eliezer:
one day, one may not establish an eiruv for half
half of it to the south?
Just as one may not establish an eiruv for one day, half
to the south, so too, one may not establish an eiruv for two
one day to the east and one day to the west.
Don’t you concede that if one established an eiruv with his feet
the first day … establish … eiruv with his feet on … the second day,
the first day and remaining there during the twilight period, as opposed to depositing food there beforehand, he nonetheless must establish another eiruv with his feet on the eve of the second day,
his eiruv was eaten on the first day, he may not … on it … go out
his eiruv was eaten on the first day, he may not rely on it and go out
said to him: … Indeed, … said to them: … isn’t it
said to him: Indeed, that is correct. Rabbi Eliezer then said to them: Then isn’t it
